cases.name: async-foreach-does-not-wait
cases.trap: forEach ignores returned Promises, so the outer function can finish before saves finish and rejections may be unowned.
cases.prompt: Fix: `async function saveAll(items){ items.forEach(async item => { await save(item) }); }`. The contract requires saveAll to resolve only after every save succeeds, failing if any save fails.
expectations: Replaces async forEach with an owned Promise pattern such as awaiting Promise.all over mapped saves when saves are independent.
Makes saveAll wait for all requested work under the stated fail-fast contract.
Keeps save rejections attached to saveAll rather than floating.

cases.name: revalidate-state-after-await
cases.trap: A pre-await generation or current pointer can become stale while external work is in flight.
cases.prompt: A cache refresh reads `const generation = state.generation`, awaits fetchRemote(), then always writes the result into state. Another refresh may advance generation while the fetch is pending. What must the implementation do?
expectations: Recognizes that shared state may change across await.
Re-checks a generation/token/current request identity before committing, or serializes through an existing accepted mutation boundary.
Prevents an older completion from overwriting newer state.

cases.name: promise-race-timeout-does-not-cancel-loser
cases.trap: Promise.race returns a timeout but the underlying request continues and may later mutate state.
cases.prompt: Review a timeout helper implemented as `await Promise.race([fetchAndApply(), delay(1000).then(() => { throw new Error('timeout') })])`. Is the operation actually stopped at one second?
expectations: Explains that Promise.race does not cancel the losing fetchAndApply operation.
Uses AbortController or another supported cancellation mechanism, or otherwise suppresses/guards late effects.
Cleans up timeout resources or listeners when the main operation wins.

cases.name: best-effort-needs-all-outcomes
cases.trap: Promise.all fails fast and stops reporting later outcomes even though every notification result is required.
cases.prompt: Send 20 independent notifications. The requirement is: attempt every notification and return one success/failure result per recipient. Which Promise pattern fits and why?
expectations: Uses Promise.allSettled or an equivalent explicit per-item error collector because all outcomes must be observed.
Does not use fail-fast Promise.all as the sole collector under this requirement.
Still considers bounded concurrency if the collection size or resource cost warrants it.
